prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1322; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- Nobody gave the claimant's name at the scene; the claimant joined the claim days later.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red light in Pasadena, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling at a speed consistent with the impact described by both drivers. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder at the scene and stated that the seatbelt tightened hard across the chest on impact. A Passenger seated in the front right seat reported no injury. Two witnesses standing at the adjacent bus stop told me they saw Driver 2 fail to slow in time, and photographs taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper and trunk area that is largely consistent with the force described. Driver 2 acknowledged the collision without dispute. Some small, weathered scratches on the rear panel appeared older than the recent damage and were noted but not attributed to this event. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Driver 1 did not provide identifying details at the scene, and a claim was filed with the insurer several days later. Injury reported appears plausible given the mechanism of this collision. No citations were issued at the scene.
